'''''Filago vulgaris''''' or '''''Filago germanica''''',<ref name="itiscol">{{ITIS|id=37374|taxon=''Filago vulgaris''}}</ref> commonly known as '''common cudweed''' or '''common cottonrose''', is an annual [[herbaceous plant]] of the genus ''[[Filago (plant)|Filago]]''.<ref name="usda">{{PLANTS|symbol=Fivu2 |taxon=Filago vulgaris (common cottonrose)}}</ref> It is in the tribe [[Inuleae]] of the 
sunflower family, [[Asteraceae]]. Common names also include: [[Danish language|Danish]]—''Kugle-museurt'', and [[Norwegian language|Norwegian]]—''Kuleullurt''.<ref name="cabi">[http://www.cabi.org/isc/?compid=5&dsid=114405&loadmodule=datasheet&page=481&site=144 Cabi.org—Invasive Species Compendium | ''Filago vulgaris'']</ref>

==Distribution==
''Filago vulgaris'' is native to Europe, from the [[Mediterranean region]] north to [[Northern Ireland]], [[Scotland]]. It is found in [[grassland]], [[sand dune]]s, rocky ledges, and cultivated fields.<ref name="itiscol"/><ref>[http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/filago-vulgaris Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora — ''Filago vulgaris''] . accessed 4.4.2013</ref> It is a listed [[Near Threatened]] species in the Red Data Book for [[England]], due to agricultural practices.<ref name="dorset">[http://www.dorsetnature.co.uk/pages-flower/wf-106.html Dorset: ''F. vulgaris'']</ref>

It is a naturalized [[introduced species]] in the Northwestern and [[Eastern United States]], and in [[British Columbia]] and [[Ontario]], Canada.<ref name="usda"/>

;Description
''Filago vulgaris'' can reach {{convert|5|-|30|cm|in}} in height. The linear wavy-edged leaves and the stems are a white and woolly in texture and appearance.<ref name="dorset"/>

The plant blooms July to September, with dense, terminal flowerheads, flowers that are light yellow.<ref name="dorset"/>
